name: Warrior
summary: Across Azeroth, Warriors take their place at the front with steel, discipline, and battle rage. They wear heavy plate and wield many weapons, shielding allies or breaking enemy ranks. Every race and civilization has its Warriors, from city guards and royal champions to wandering mercenaries.

sections.title: Masters of Steel and Shield
sections.body: Warriors rely on strength, discipline, and skill with weapons, not prayers or spells. Heavy plate helps them hold the front. Some brace behind tall shields, enduring blows and drawing danger away from spellcasters and archers. Others carry two-handed polearms, axes, or greatswords. Some fight with a blade in each hand and cut through enemy ranks.

sections.title: The Power of Battle Rage
sections.body: In battle, pain and blood kindle a Warrior's rage. It grows as Warriors strike foes and endure their attacks. Skilled fighters shape that force into crushing blows and sweeping weapon strikes. Their battle cries hearten nearby allies and break enemy morale.

sections.title: A Universal Tradition
sections.body:
Every race on Azeroth has its Warriors. Stormwind fields disciplined knights and footmen, while Ironforge calls on its stout mountain guard. The Horde rallies around orcish blademasters, tauren braves, and Forsaken Deathguards.

Honor, defense of their lands, or the promise of coin can lead Warriors to arms. They form the backbone of every standing army.

faq.q: What powers a warrior if they do not use magic?
faq.answer: Warriors draw strength from martial skill, training, and rage. They build rage by striking foes and taking blows, then unleash it in sweeping attacks, shield strikes, and fierce shouts.
Every race in Azeroth can become a Warrior. All mortal cultures need armored fighters at the front, from the dwarven defenders of Khaz Modan to the orcish shock troops of Durotar.

faq.q: What role do warriors serve in a combat party?
faq.answer: Warriors usually fight at the front. Those who favor protection use plate and shields to endure attacks and keep dangerous foes focused on them. Those who favor arms or fury wield heavy two-handed weapons or paired blades to overwhelm enemies with physical force.

faq.q: What weapons are warriors able to wield?
faq.answer: Warriors wield almost every weapon used in mortal warfare: swords, maces, axes, polearms, daggers, and staves, either one-handed or two-handed. They also carry heavy shields and use bows, guns, and crossbows.

faq.q: Who are some famous warriors in Azeroth's history?
faq.answer: Renowned Warriors include Lord Anduin Lothar, Champion of Stormwind and Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron; Grommash Hellscream, chieftain of the Warsong clan; and Cairne Bloodhoof, High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes.

faq.q: Where do new warriors receive their formal training?
faq.answer: Warriors train wherever soldiers gather. Human recruits drill in Northshire Abbey; dwarves and gnomes learn at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley; and night elves train in Shadowglen. Orcs and trolls practice in the Valley of Trials, Forsaken fighters report to the Deathknell barracks, and the Skyborne begin on Zephras Isle.

angles.text: Every battle tests your stamina and nerve. Turn the pain of incoming blows into rage, and you can hold the front line.
As a Warrior, you rely on blacksmiths for heavy plate, sturdy bucklers, and keen blades to help you survive combat.
As an Alliance Warrior, you join the footmen and knights who defend human kingdoms, dwarven mountain holds, and elven forests.
As a Horde Warrior, you join a martial way of life, where grunt shock troops and tauren fighters lead each territorial advance.
